title: Power
description: A force or tech power: the SW5e replacement for spells. Force powers are fuelled by force points and carry a light or dark alignment; tech powers are fuelled by tech points and never do. The header fields below are what a player reads mid-combat, so every one of them should be answerable without opening the description.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this power. Derived from the name once and never reused, so saved characters keep resolving after a rename.

name.description: Display name. Stored in title case; render it lowercase and italic when it is referenced from inside another power's text, as the books do.

powerType.description: Which casting system the power belongs to. This decides the point pool it spends, the casting ability, and whether forceAlignment applies.

level.description: Power level. Level 0 is an at-will power that costs no points and scales with character level; levels 1 to 9 cost that many points to cast at their base level.

forceAlignment.description: Where the power sits on the light-dark axis, which governs who may learn it and whether casting it costs dark side points. Universal powers are available to any force user. Tech powers always record none.

castingTime.description: How long casting takes, split into the machine-readable period a turn tracker needs and the printed phrasing a player reads.

period.description: The unit of the casting time. Use reaction for powers with a trigger and none for powers that are not cast in the usual sense.

text.description: The casting time exactly as printed, including the quantity and, for reactions, the trigger: "1 reaction, which you take when you take kinetic damage".

range.description: Range as printed, including any area of effect in parentheses: "90 feet", "Self (15-foot cone)", "Touch".

duration.description: How long the effect lasts as printed, for example Instantaneous, 1 round, or Up to 1 minute. Record concentration separately rather than folding it in here.

concentration.description: Whether maintaining the power requires concentration, so a character sheet can drop it automatically when a new concentration power is cast or a save is failed. Always present, including when false.

prerequisite.description: What a character must already have to learn this power, typically a prerequisite power or a minimum level. Omit when there is none.

description.description: Markdown rules text in second person, describing what happens on a cast. Where the effect scales, the archived corpus writes the scaling into the closing paragraph of this text rather than into a separate field.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this power was published in, matching a document of the source content type. Values present in the archive are phb and ec.

contentSet.description: Whether this power belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.
